# Las versiones del mar

`BUTTON[read-today]`

# Text

**The Versions of the Sea**

Few questions belong to writing as closely as the one a translation
poses.[^1] Habit, pride and caution all shape the answer.

> The gulls went over and the water stayed,
> the boat came home without the man who rowed,
> and on the beach a child still played
> with the long rope the morning owed.

The first version is literal; the second, it must be said, is not.

> When the tide had turned, the harbor slept,
> and the lamps were lit along the quay;
> [a gloss: the quay is the old one, since demolished]

The two versions differ in nearly every word, yet a reader moving between them
loses less than one would fear.

---

[^1]: The question is older than the essay suggests; it is at least as old as the
first bilingual editions.

    A second paragraph of the note continues here, indented four spaces, as

    > The rope is long, the morning short,
    > and every version leaves the port.
